title: Orchestration-led PRD for chat+embeddings+rerank MVP and launch readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a minimal, production-safe bundle that exposes chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank in a single orchestrated hosted surface. This PRD clarifies behavior contracts, mandatory acceptance gates, and a staged rollout plan that minimizes customer impact while enabling high-throughput patterns (batching, prefix caching) in the runtime. The doc reconciles product constraints (single API surface, consistent behavioral guarantees) with engineering constraints (backward-compatible request/response formats, incremental model variants, autoscaling profiles).
scope: In-scope: unified endpoint surface (single URL) supporting chat messages and single-turn completions, embeddings vector generation, and basic rerank API. Behavioral contracts for deterministic top-k rerank, embedding dimensional stability, and chat streaming. Acceptance telemetry and canary gating. Out-of-scope: multimodal inputs, advanced rerank learning-to-rank features, model training components, and private/VPC deployment packaging (handled in a follow-up ticket).
out_of_scope: Fine-grained L2 rerank tuning, custom model hosting for customer-provided models, and on-prem install artifacts are explicitly out-of-scope for this MVP.
acceptance_criteria: API surface conforms to the swagger contract in linked spec and passes contract tests (back-compat/forward-compat vectors)
Latency SLOs: p50 <= 120ms for embeddings on standard unit, p50 <= 180ms for chat short-seq on dedicated lane; p99 subject to runtime autoscaler behavior documented in rollout notes
Throughput: deduced burst capacity and steady-state throughput validated in load tests per runbook
Quality: embedding cosine stability across minor model pin updates within 0.02 average delta on benchmark prompt set
Rerank deterministic behavior for identical input batch and model variant (no flakiness) validated in 1000-sample regression suite
End-to-end telemetry present: token cost breakdown, per-request model variant, batching delta, and KV cache hit ratio
Canary plan executed: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with rollback hooks and automated regression checks
Documentation: SDK examples, example prompts, and known-limits table published to docs.redwood.com before GA
Security: KMS-backed key access verified for logging and customer data masking enabled for PII in telemetry streams
Operational: alerting for error rate, model fallback rate, and autoscaler latency breaches provisioned in console dashboards
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 - Internal dogfood: routing 100% internal org traffic to new surface; gather debug traces and internal evals (2 days)
Phase 1 - Canary: 5% production traffic, run automated behavioral regression and pricing telemetry (3 days)
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 25% then 75% with manual checkpoints and QA signoffs (2x 2-day windows)
Phase 3 - GA cutover: 100% and retire deprecated endpoint after 48h of stable telemetry
telemetry_requirements: Per-request model_variant, model_revision, lane (hosted/dedicated), and routing_reason
Token-level cost breakdown surfaced in trace and aggregated dashboards
Batching statistics: mean/percentile batch size and latency contribution
KV cache metrics: hit/miss ratio, prefix cache usage, and corresponding latency delta
Quality metrics: embedding drift score, rerank flip-rate, and response stability index
migration_plan: Provide an automated migration helper that rewrites old endpoint params to the new unified surface where feasible; maintain compatibility layer for 60 days. Send alert to customers using deprecated fields and instrument telemetry to detect unmigrated callers. Engineering to publish an upgrade guide with example SDK patches and compatibility tests.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: behavioral regressions after model pin swap. Mitigation: pre-rollout regression suite with holdout prompts and automatic rollback on threshold breaches
Risk: cost spike due to unexpected batching behavior. Mitigation: synthetic load tests and early throttling policy with circuit-breaker to default lower-cost model variants
Risk: telemetry gap around KV cache. Mitigation: dry-run KV instrumentation turned on in dogfood stage and block GA until coverage >= 95%
Risk: customer confusion over response format. Mitigation: publish mapping table and maintain backward-compatible response fields for 60 days
qa_checklist: Run full contract tests (back-compat/forward-compat) and record results
Execute load profile A/B comparisons and validate throughput and p99 behavior
End-to-end fuzzing for input permutations and streaming edge cases
Telem assert: KV cache, batching, and token cost fields present in traces
Smoke test SDK examples across Python, JS, and Go
Security scan for logging PII exposures and verify KMS key rotation works
